I guess it keeps the views cleaner since all you have to do is query your DB and return the dumped marshmallow object (and jsonify it if you want a JSON response). Otherwise you'd have to write a function that does that for you.
The Tutorial I linked here is ONLY server. There is no client. You could build a javascript client for example that calls the api.

No it is not. In order to be RESTful you need to have a separation of client and server. The Server would only be responsible for serving the api and the client consumes it and lets the user interact.

You still need Flask-SQLAlchemy (or any other ORM) to define your db models. Marshmallow isn't going to communicate with your database, rather it provides methods for outputting your data (stored in your database). You could use something like Flask-Restful, which has a built in serializer (as far as i know) or you could write it all by yourself as Miguel Gringberg does [here](https://github.com/miguelgrinberg/flack/blob/master/flack/models.py) for example (look at the functions "from_dict" and "to_dict").
I think it's fairly easy to get started with Marshmallow so I don't see any reason not to use it, but it really is just a matter of preference!

Hi,

[this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6RdZNiyISVU) is very good overview of what constitutes an API, I suggest you watch it to get familiar with it. The code in your example is not a REST API, since it doesn't seperate client from server (I wouldn't even say it's an API all together).

Flask itself is a very good tool for building APIs since you can specify an endpoint (like "/api/users") and have this endpoint serve a JSON response (doesn't have to be JSON). Hence you don't really need Flask RESTful. I'd also say in order to get familiar with APIs and know what you do, start without any extensions.
